frase_gancho.texto: The sacred word that blossoms in festivals, cornfields, and shared rituals.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Conclude your ethnographic journey by exploring the hall dedicated to the Nahua people, the most numerous and widespread Indigenous group in Mexico. Direct heirs of the Uto-Aztecan language and of the Mesoamerican cultural matrix, the Nahua live in many states of the Mexican Republic. This gallery showcases the richness of the festive calendar, where requests for rain on sacred hills, the dances of the Moors and Christians, and the colorful Xantolo celebrations for the dead stand out. The space highlights how clothing, traditional music, and oral tradition in Nahuatl continue to be the fundamental pillar that preserves community cohesion.
